questions.prompt: Pasteur's fermentation research showed that a living organism (yeast) causes a specific chemical change. How did this finding directly support the later Germ Theory of Disease?

options.text: It proved bacteria could survive boiling
It established that a specific living microbe could cause a specific effect — a concept later extended to disease
It disproved spontaneous generation directly
It identified antibiotics for the first time

questions.explanation: Showing that yeast (a living microbe) causes fermentation, and bacteria cause spoilage, built the conceptual bridge to microbes causing disease.

questions.prompt: Which flaw in Spallanzani's sealed-flask experiment did Pasteur's swan-necked flask correct, finally disproving spontaneous generation?

options.text: Spallanzani's broth was never boiled
Spallanzani's sealed flask kept out air entirely, so critics argued a "vital force" was blocked; Pasteur's design let air in while still keeping microbes out
Spallanzani used gelatin instead of broth
Spallanzani's flask lacked a swan neck for measuring temperature

questions.explanation: Pasteur's swan-necked design let air (and any "vital force") reach the broth while gravity trapped microbes in the curve of the neck, isolating the true cause of contamination.

questions.prompt: Lactobacillus acidophilus helps prevent vaginal yeast infections caused by Candida albicans (from Module 1). Why would a healthy population of Lactobacillus reduce that risk?

options.text: Lactobacillus directly injects antibiotics into Candida
Lactobacillus produces lactic acid, creating conditions that compete with and limit the growth of Candida albicans
Lactobacillus and Candida albicans are the same species
Candida albicans cannot survive around any bacteria at all

questions.explanation: Lactobacillus is described as a beneficial, lactic-acid-producing probiotic that helps prevent yeast infections — its metabolic activity limits the environment Candida needs to overgrow.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the Golden Age of Microbiology is FALSE?

options.text: It spanned roughly the mid-1800s to early 1900s.
Scientists during this era worked to answer whether life arises spontaneously.
This era addressed what causes fermentation.
This era occurred before Leeuwenhoek observed bacteria.
This era addressed what causes disease and how it can be prevented.

questions.explanation: False — the Golden Age came roughly 200 years AFTER Leeuwenhoek's 1670s observations, not before.

questions.prompt: Explain the chain of contributions from Redi, to Spallanzani, to Pasteur that ultimately disproved spontaneous generation.
questions.explanation: Redi suspected microorganisms might cause meat spoilage. Spallanzani showed boiling sterilizes broth (a sealed flask stayed sterile, an open one grew microbes), but critics argued the seal blocked a "vital force." Pasteur's swan-necked flask let air in while trapping incoming microbes in the bend, finally proving microorganisms — not spontaneous generation — caused contamination.

questions.prompt: Which pairing of scientist to contribution toward combatting disease is correct?

options.text: Semmelweis discovered Penicillin
Fleming promoted hospital cleanliness
Lister pioneered the development of germicides
Nightingale emphasized hand washing

questions.explanation: Lister pioneered germicides. (Semmelweis = hand washing; Nightingale = hospital cleanliness; Fleming = Penicillin.)

questions.prompt: If a hospital wanted to combine the insights of Semmelweis, Nightingale, and Lister to reduce infections, which three practices would they adopt together?

options.text: Antibiotics, vaccines, and pasteurization
Hand washing, hospital cleanliness, and germicide use
Genetic engineering, fermentation control, and refrigeration
Binomial naming, taxonomy, and microscopy

questions.explanation: Semmelweis (hand washing), Nightingale (hospital cleanliness), and Lister (germicides) together cover these three practices.

questions.prompt: Fleming's discovery of Penicillin came after the Germ Theory was established. Why was the Germ Theory a necessary precondition for antibiotic discovery to be meaningful?

options.text: Without knowing microbes cause disease, there would be no clear target for a disease-fighting substance
Penicillin was actually discovered before the Germ Theory
Antibiotics have nothing to do with microorganisms
Fleming needed Pasteur's swan-necked flask design specifically

questions.explanation: An antibiotic is only a meaningful concept once you know a living microorganism is the thing causing the disease in the first place.

questions.prompt: How does genetic engineering, as described in this module, exemplify a "beneficial" use of microorganisms that is distinct from fermentation-based food production?
questions.explanation: Genetic engineering manipulates a microorganism's genes so it produces a specific desired protein (such as insulin) for human use, rather than relying on the microbe's natural fermentation byproducts (like alcohol or CO2), as in food production.

questions.prompt: Cyanobacteria and Lactobacillus acidophilus are both described as beneficial in this module. What is the key functional difference between their roles?

options.text: Cyanobacteria decompose dead matter; Lactobacillus produces oxygen
Cyanobacteria produce oxygen via photosynthesis; Lactobacillus produces lactic acid as a probiotic
They perform the exact same function
Cyanobacteria are pathogenic while Lactobacillus is not

questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria contribute atmospheric oxygen through photosynthesis; Lactobacillus contributes lactic acid that supports a healthy vaginal environment — very different beneficial mechanisms.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Pasteur's contributions across this module is FALSE?

options.text: He showed yeast causes fermentation.
He proposed the Germ Theory of Disease.
He performed the rigorous experimental proof that established the Germ Theory beyond doubt.
He designed the swan-necked flask experiment.
He is associated with pasteurization.

questions.explanation: False — Robert Koch (not Pasteur) performed the rigorous experimental proof; Pasteur proposed the idea.

questions.prompt: A dairy company wants to reduce microbial load in milk without fully sterilizing it (to preserve taste). Which process, developed by the scientist behind the Germ Theory, should they use?

options.text: Autoclaving
Pasteurization
Genetic engineering
Binomial classification

questions.explanation: Pasteurization (developed by Pasteur) reduces microbial load while preserving product quality.

questions.prompt: Saccharomyces cerevisiae ferments sugar into CO2 and ethanol. Which correctly identifies two different beneficial products of this single organism's activity, based on this module?

options.text: Insulin and Penicillin
Bread (from CO2) and alcohol (from ethanol)
Yogurt and cheese
Oxygen and nutrients

questions.explanation: The same fermentation reaction's two products — CO2 and ethanol — are responsible for leavened bread and alcoholic beverages, respectively.

questions.prompt: Which of these four scientists worked on disproving spontaneous generation, rather than combatting disease directly in a hospital setting?

options.text: Semmelweis
Lister
Spallanzani
Nightingale

questions.explanation: Spallanzani's sealed-vs-open flask experiment addressed spontaneous generation; the other three worked on hospital infection control.

questions.prompt: Louis Pasteur's fermentation work and his Germ Theory work both rely on the same core insight. What is that shared insight?

options.text: Boiling always sterilizes completely
A specific living microorganism can be responsible for a specific observable effect
All microorganisms are harmful
Antibiotics kill all microbes

questions.explanation: Whether it's yeast causing fermentation or a pathogen causing disease, the underlying insight is the same: a specific living microbe produces a specific effect.
